clue.text: Daily woman on way in to have a flutter

indicators.note: the woman-on-the-way combination is placed inside the word for a wager

parts.note: to have a flutter is to place a small bet

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: a road is a way
she is a woman's pronoun

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady on her way in for a small wager on the horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like the charwoman but is the newspaper; 'on' sets the woman after the way, and 'in' puts that pair inside the wager. A broadsheet is a large-format, traditionally serious paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a full-size newspaper, and a daily is a paper published every day.

clue.text: Think of an explanation

definitions.meaning: to think logically, to work things out in the mind
a cause or justification given for something

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to think things through logically; as a noun it means the cause offered to explain something.

clue.text: After the Fall, man is past his prime

indicators.note: the man's name is placed after the season in the answer

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: After the Fall of Eden, mankind is in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Fall' suggests the biblical story, but it is simply the season, as Americans call it.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumnal describes the later, declining stage of life, beyond one's best years.

clue.text: Inferior alternative makes a decent boss distraught

indicators.note: distraught means wildly upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Settling for a lesser option drives a fair-minded manager to despair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-best is a lesser option, not the first choice.

clue.text: Most men are taken by this stage in Beckett's work

definitions.text: Most men are taken by this stage
definitions.meaning: in chess, by the final phase of a game most pieces have been captured

explanation.definitionFit: It is the closing phase of a chess game, when few pieces remain, and the title of a Samuel Beckett play.

clue.text: Starts to train Arsenal team to make progress along the ground

indicators.note: the opening letters of the following words are taken

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: Football training tips for Arsenal's first team on moving up the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; the football setting hides an aircraft's ground movement.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft taxis when it moves slowly on the runway before take-off or after landing.

clue.text: Romeo's friend found out crime was bad

indicators.note: the letters behaving badly are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend of Romeo discovered that wrongdoing was evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercutio is Romeo's witty companion in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Deliberately deprived me for certain of son

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: deprived of means losing something, so the son's letter is removed

parts.note: assuredly means for certain

explanation.surface: Someone complains they've definitely been robbed of their boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived' with its 'of' tells you to remove the son's letter from the synonym for certain, leaving ASUREDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something measuredly is doing it in a careful, considered way.

clue.text: French physicist was a politician before

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A scientist from France had once been in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double service in the surface, but in the parse it is just the letter A, with MP the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: André-Marie Ampère was the French scientist after whom the unit of electric current is named.

clue.text: Taken round the room and grilled

indicators.note: the word for taken goes around the room

parts.note: led means taken or guided
an attic is a room in the roof

explanation.surface: Someone escorted round the room and closely questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grilled' suggests interrogation but means fitted with a grille.
explanation.definitionFit: Latticed means fitted with a crisscross framework, like a grille.

clue.text: Ugly expressions of serious champions

parts.note: grim means stern and serious
aces are experts or champions

explanation.surface: Sour faces from stern winners.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a contorted facial expression of pain or disgust.

clue.text: A Name working incognito briefly

parts.note: on means functioning or working

explanation.surface: A named person operating under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' belongs to the definition: the short form of anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is a short form of anonymous, describing someone who keeps their identity hidden.

clue.text: Prosecuting in a case

definitions.meaning: in grammar, in the case used for the direct object

explanation.definitionFit: The word means making an accusation, and is also the grammatical case for a verb's direct object.

clue.text: Rather stupid, to hang around inside for a lift

indicators.note: the waiting goes inside the comparative of stupid

parts.note: dumber means more stupid
to wait is to hang around

explanation.surface: Someone too dim to do anything but wait indoors for a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a small lift for carrying food or dishes between floors.

clue.text: Make Whip repeat changes to published policy

indicators.note: the words are changed, their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A party whip is told to say it again, and alters the government's stated position.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip is the party official who enforces voting discipline in the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A white paper is a UK government document setting out proposed policy.

clue.text: Hardy creditor comes round to see working man

indicators.note: the creditor's abbreviation goes round the comedian's name

parts.note: Oliver (Ollie) Hardy of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: A tough lender calls on a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' reads as tough but is the comedian Oliver Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, a classic manual labourer.

clue.text: Pork in dripping, and port

indicators.note: the pig goes inside the cooking fat

parts.note: dripping is fat from roast meat, like lard
boar is a pig, the source of pork

explanation.surface: Cooking pork in its fat, with a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink but is the ship's left side.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the old nautical term for the left-hand side of a ship.

clue.text: Daughter, not a virgin, had to return such a ring

indicators.note: the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a maid is a virgin, so not a virgin is no maid

explanation.surface: A daughter who lost her innocence had to give back the engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had to return' turns D + NO MAID round, so the whole run is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring set with a precious gemstone is named after the stone.

clue.text: Said to make fun of an evil that's afoot

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: to mock a sin is to make fun of a wrong

explanation.surface: Ridiculing wickedness is said to be what's going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' suggests something happening, but means worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft leather shoe, worn on the foot.

clue.text: The first woman to have a troublesome chest …

definitions.text: The first woman to have a troublesome chest

parts.words: The first woman to have a troublesome chest
parts.note: reads like a woman with a cough, but describes the first woman in Greek myth, given a jar or box that released the world's troubles

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was the first mortal woman, whose opened box let evils loose on the world.

clue.text: Joker put on games clothes for erotic entertainment

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: a team's strip is its sports kit
a tease is someone who jokes or teases

explanation.surface: A prankster puts on sports kit for an adult show.
explanation.walkthrough: A strip is the British word for a team's sports kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is a performance in which someone undresses to entertain.

clue.text: Warm and comfortable, but function unknown

parts.note: cos is the cosine function in trigonometry
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Snug and comfortable, but of no clear use.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy describes somewhere snug and homely.

clue.text: … cut down chesty trouble here

indicators.note: the word is in trouble, its letters disturbed

explanation.surface: Continuing the myth: a chest problem is cut short here.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots link it to 19; 'chesty trouble' suggests a cough but is the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To scythe is to mow with a long curved blade.

clue.text: Fork out here perhaps so the old can get treatment

indicators.note: the letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: Pay up so the elderly can see a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fork out' looks like paying, but is a garden fork kept out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden shed stores implements such as a fork.

clue.text: Animals obeyed call

indicators.note: the word is called out, giving a matching sound

parts.note: heard means heeded or obeyed

explanation.surface: The beasts did as they were told.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a group of cattle or similar beasts.

clue.text: Corresponding with workplace via the post office

indicators.note: via means through, so the post office goes through the middle

parts.note: op is a musical work
a site is a place
PO is the abbreviation for post office

explanation.surface: Writing to the office by post.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'workplace' supplies two pieces, a musical work and a place, which 'via' splits around the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite means matching or equivalent, as in your opposite number.

clue.text: Church official is right on the brink

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: the verge is the edge or brink

explanation.surface: A churchman is correctly on the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A verger is a church caretaker who also attends the clergy.

clue.text: Passed on one calling 'double

parts.note: dead means passed on
a ringer is one who rings or calls

explanation.surface: Someone died while phoning about a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is someone who looks exactly like another person.
